observations.behavior: Added documentation defining `SourceResponse.sort_mode` semantics (asc/desc/None) and the risks of misdeclaring order for incremental watermarks.
observations.posthog_connection: Clarifies how agents should validate row ordering before claiming `sort_mode='asc'`, preventing silent data loss in resumable syncs.
observations.code_quote: `"asc"` is a promise the pipeline relies on. After a worker shutdown, the next attempt of an `"asc"` run reads only the rows after the last value the earlier attempt queued. A row below that value that arrives later is never read, and the watermark then moves past it. A false `"asc"` loses rows silently. With `None` the interrupted run starts again from the stored watermark, which is always correct.

observations.behavior: Updated implementation guidance to require verifying API sort order against actual behavior (e.g., cursor pagination) before setting `sort_mode`.
observations.posthog_connection: Prevents agents from assuming ascending order on APIs that may return newest-first or ignore sort params, which would corrupt watermarks.
observations.code_quote: - **`sort_mode` must match the order rows actually arrive in — verify it, don't assume it.** The pipeline trusts `sort_mode="asc"` to checkpoint the incremental watermark after every batch and to allow safe mid-sync worker shutdowns; declaring `asc` while the API returns newest-first corrupts the watermark and breaks resume semantics. Check the API's _default_ sort (it applies when you can't pass `sort`), and remember cursor pagination often rejects or ignores sort params entirely.

observations.behavior: Updated troubleshooting guide to include specific failure modes related to incorrect `sort_mode` declarations.
observations.posthog_connection: Helps operators identify why incremental syncs might skip data or re-fetch history due to mismatched sort assumptions.
observations.code_quote: - `sort_mode="asc"` declared on an API that returns newest-first: a run that continues after a mid-sync shutdown skips the older rows it did not read yet. Declare `"desc"`, or `None` when the order is not known.
